daily_brief: Ukraine struck a critical blow against Russian logistics by severely damaging the Crimean Bridge in what President Zelensky described as an 'unprecedented operation,' causing a major section to collapse into the water [BBC, Al Jazeera, ABC Australia]. The timing is significant as the strike precedes a rare trilateral summit between Presidents Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen this week, drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia]. Meanwhile, the fallout from the Nvidia scandal continues to shape US-China tech relations, with Washington announcing new restrictions on remote access to AI chips through third-country data centres [The Hindu, Al Jazeera, BBC]. In Europe, five EU member states announced joint negotiations with Rwanda to establish deportation centres for rejected asylum seekers [The Guardian, RFI], while French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen signalled she would end financial aid to Ukraine if elected [RFI]. The Quad leaders met in Manila, unveiling new defence cooperation and critical minerals agreements aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence [ABC Australia, Nikkei Asia, The Hindu].

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Inflicts Major Damage on Crimean Bridge in 'Unprecedented' Strike
bullets: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, causing a large arched section to collapse into the water
President Zelensky said the attack followed weeks of methodically destroying Russian air defences, radar systems, and electronic warfare capabilities
Russia's Crimea governor reported two deaths and suspended all traffic across the 19-kilometre road and rail bridge
The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed and vowed to rebuild the bridge 'better than before'

top_stories.headline: Xi, Trump, and Putin to Hold Trilateral Summit at APEC, Drawing Yalta Comparisons
bullets: Chinese Foreign Ministry confirmed a trilateral meeting of Chinese, US, and Russian presidents will occur Thursday in Shenzhen following the APEC summit
China described the meeting as 'of groundbreaking significance' for 'safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability'
Russia's chief negotiator has called for new European security arrangements as part of a 'modern Yalta' framework
Smaller nations and analysts have expressed concern the three nuclear powers could reach agreements ignoring other countries' interests

top_stories.headline: US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls Amid Nvidia Scandal Fallout
bullets: US announced new regulations requiring licences for remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third countries, targeting Chinese firms
The rules were written by Treasury and the White House rather than Commerce, reflecting reported tensions between Secretaries Bessent and Lutnick
US confirmed ongoing investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed since 2024 for potential export control violations involving Nvidia chips
China condemned the restrictions as 'abusing export control measures'; announcement came days before Trump-Xi summit

top_stories.headline: Five EU States Launch Joint Negotiations with Rwanda for Migrant Deportation Centre
bullets: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark, and Greece are negotiating with Rwanda to establish a centre for migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected
The pilot scheme would accommodate around 100 adults who have exhausted all legal appeals, excluding minors
Unlike the failed UK-Rwanda scheme, this would not apply to people still pursuing asylum claims
45 human rights organisations criticised the plans in a joint letter, while Rwanda's interior minister said it offers migrants a 'second chance'

top_stories.headline: Quad Leaders Announce Defence and Critical Minerals Cooperation at Manila Summit
bullets: US, Australia, India, and Japan held their first leaders-level Quad meeting in two years on the sidelines of ASEAN summit in Manila
Trump announced new critical minerals deals and joint military exercises featuring maritime patrol aircraft
Leaders issued joint statement opposing 'destabilising or unilateral actions' and expressing concerns about 'economic coercion' including arbitrary export restrictions
Australia's PM Albanese will travel to Shenzhen for expected meeting with Chinese President Xi
